summary.text: A traditional Rocky Roquemore par 72, opened in 2002, in an unspoilt, quieter part of the eastern Algarve.

setting.text: Set in the Ria Formosa Natural Park, with sweeping views of the Atlantic and Cacela Velha beach.
Sits within the Ria Formosa Natural Park, a protected wetland and one of the Algarve's most important ecosystems.
The park is a line of barrier islands along the coast; the course has sea views, sandy beach islands and mountains on the other side.
A fairly flat parkland course where there is usually a breeze to cope with.
The front nine is tree-lined and tight; from the 11th the course opens out and plays nearer the sea, and the challenges get more interesting.
Over 300 olive, cork and carob trees line the course.

history.text: Opened in 2002, a few months before neighbouring sister course Quinta de Cima.
Part of a protected stretch known locally as the Sotavento, which keeps the course free of villa-lined fairways.

trivia.text: Two loops of nine, each with two par 5s, five par 4s and two par 3s.
Five man-made lakes provide the course's hazards and its irrigation.
Measures 6,016 metres from the back tees.
Top100golfcourses ranks it 25th in Portugal and 11th in the Algarve.
Construction around the course is restricted to protect the environment.

1.text: A welcoming, wide par 5 to start.
A formidable bunker looms on the left.

2.text: A gentle par 3 of about 150 yards, but the green slopes hard from back to front: go past the hole and an early three-putt beckons.

5.text: A par 3 with two teeing areas, both asking for a shot over a lake to a shallow green guarded by bunkers.

10.text: 'A killer hole': a 422-metre par 4 with out of bounds all down the left and a large lake guarding the green from 100 metres out. A par is worth celebrating.
Probably the signature hole, where the course picks up momentum after the turn.

11.text: A sweeping par 5, gently uphill then down, where the course opens out towards the sea.

12.text: A scenic short par 4 with the sea on the left and palm trees framing the front of the green.

13.text: A long par 3 running parallel with the Ria Formosa, into the prevailing wind, to a green just 22 metres wide almost encircled by bunkers.

14.text: A left-to-right dogleg par 4 around a lake.

16.text: 'A potential card-wrecker': a par 5 that doglegs right then left between the two biggest lakes to a green tucked just behind the second.
With the 17th, the signature holes, carved through the lakes; they can make or break a round.

17.text: The green is bordered by a lake holding an island with a variety of birdlife.

18.text: A more conventional par 4 of about 420 yards to a well-protected green.

local.text: In the Sotavento, the eastern Algarve, 12km from Tavira.
Just over 30 minutes from Faro airport.
Close to the Spanish border, so the Isla Canela courses in Spain are within reach.
